description: Realistic evaluation scenarios for the barbershop-crm-builder skill. Each scenario has a prompt, expected behaviors (success criteria) and explicit failure signals that indicate the skill was not followed.

evaluations.prompt: Build a booking website for a small barbershop with three barbers, a handful of services, and Google Sheets as the CRM.
success_criteria: Gathers or explicitly marks pending real business data (name, address, timezone, currency, prices, hours, staff) instead of inventing plausible values.
Records an explicit architecture decision (spreadsheet-backed CRM) with stated reasoning, not a silent default.
Writes availability rules in prose before implementing them.
Designs a CRM schema with snapshotting on appointments and idempotent setup.
Implements the availability engine as read-only and the confirmation path as a locked, re-validated mutation.
The booking website calls only this project's own backend API, never the CRM/spreadsheet backend directly.
Includes a concurrency test proving two simultaneous bookings for the same slot cannot both succeed.
Final report distinguishes implemented / verified-with-mocks / verified-locally / verified-against-real-service honestly.
failure_signals: Invents a plausible-looking price list, hours, or barber bios and presents them as real business data.
Frontend code calls a spreadsheet or CRM API directly instead of a backend layer.
No test exercises concurrent booking attempts for the identical slot.
Claims the booking flow is 'production-verified' without ever calling a real deployed CRM backend.
Ships a static/demo booking form with no real availability engine behind it.

evaluations.prompt: We already have a nice-looking website with a booking page, but the booking flow is simulated. Connect it to a real backend/CRM.
success_criteria: Preserves the existing visual design instead of rebuilding it.
Audits the current simulated flow before writing integration code.
Introduces (or reuses) a backend API layer; the frontend never calls the CRM/spreadsheet backend directly.
Replaces hardcoded services/staff/slots with real API-sourced data.
Adds loading/empty/error states that the simulated version never needed.
Adds a client-generated idempotency key to the real booking submission.
Handles SLOT_UNAVAILABLE by returning to the date/time step and preserving already-entered customer data.
Does not rewrite unrelated parts of the website that already worked.
failure_signals: Rebuilds the site's visual design or copy without being asked to.
Leaves the frontend calling the CRM/spreadsheet backend directly, citing 'it already worked that way'.
No idempotency key on the real appointment-creation call.
SLOT_UNAVAILABLE is unhandled or clears the customer's already-entered data.
Hardcoded demo services/staff/slots remain in the shipped frontend after the change.

evaluations.prompt: We want a booking website, an admin panel, and a WhatsApp channel, all for the same barbershop, and we're worried about double-booking across channels.
success_criteria: All three channels call the same CrmClient-shaped interface; no channel has its own availability logic.
Chat-channel webhook event deduplication is atomic (lock/transaction-guarded), not check-then-insert.
Every mutation, regardless of triggering channel, acquires a lock/transaction and re-validates before writing.
A cross-channel test proves a booking made via one channel is immediately unavailable via the other two.
A cross-channel test races two channels for the identical slot and asserts exactly one booking survives, with a graceful recovery for the loser.
Human handoff suspends automated replies but keeps recording inbound messages, and only reactivates manually.
The AI layer never creates/cancels/reschedules a booking directly — it only proposes an interpretation that goes through the same validated mutation path.
failure_signals: Each channel has its own booking/availability logic that happens to look similar.
Webhook dedup is a separate check-then-insert with no lock/transaction, allowing a race.
No test actually races two channels against the identical slot.
Automated replies continue to send while a human handoff is active.
Any code path lets the AI provider's output write an appointment without going through the same validated mutation call every other channel uses.
